However, it does mention that the net climate-change impact was −2,257.14 kg CO2-eq per t of spent FCC catalyst, indicating a net reduction in climate-change impacts. 

The document does mention that the climate-change impact of the wet-recovery stage was 1,536.56 kg CO2-eq, but after product-substitution credits, it became −1,275.04 kg CO2-eq. Similarly, the climate-change impact of the leaching-residue-valorization stage was 1,940.11 kg CO2-eq, but after product-substitution credits, it became −982.10 kg CO2-eq. 

The net climate-change impact of the integrated process is the sum of these two values, which is −2,257.14 kg CO2-eq. This suggests that the integrated route still showed a net climate-change reduction after product-substitution credits, not a net climate-change burden.
